title: Modular Tree
solution: Each operation on u is invertible (repeating it with the children frozen cycles back), and u's operations never affect its subtree, so by induction the reachable states of subtree(u) are a product: x_u ranges over the coset a_u + <g_u> in Z_{b_u}, independently of the children's reachable states. Here g_u = gcd(b_u, all achievable child sums). Child c takes values r_c + j*g_c (r_c = a_c mod g_c, 0 <= j < b_c/g_c), so the gcd of all achievable child sums is gcd(sum of r_c, g_c for every child with b_c/g_c > 1); hence g_u = gcd(b_u, S_u, G_u), computed bottom-up with a post-order DFS (a leaf gets g = b, i.e. stays fixed). Because the states are independent, every node can end at its maximum r_u + b_u - g_u simultaneously, and the answer is the sum of these. Complexity O(n log C) per test with 64-bit sums.
solution_check: true - Python implementation reproduces all 8 sample outputs and matches a BFS brute force over the full state space on 3000 random trees (n<=5, b<=6).

rejected_patterns.reason: post-order traversal is scaffolding for the bottom-up gcd aggregation, not the technique; someone searching dfs would not want this

notes.solver: Key insight: reachable set of x_u in Z_{b_u} is a coset of the subgroup generated by gcd(b_u, achievable child sums); children with a single reachable value (b_c == g_c) contribute only their fixed value to the base sum, not a step. subtree-dp would also fit; chose tree-dp as the canonical broader label. No simulation needed despite the operation-based framing.
notes.skeptic: Independently verified: implemented g_u = gcd(b_u, sum of a_c mod g_c, g_c for children with g_c < b_c), answer = sum(a_u mod g_u + b_u - g_u); matches BFS brute force over full state space on 2000 random trees (n<=5, b<=6). Reachability argument (operations are invertible group actions, parent ops never affect subtree, so states form a product) holds. subtree-dp would be an acceptable synonym for tree-dp but not needed. No binary search, no greedy, no simulation. Summary is ~62 words, third person, includes constraints; left unchanged.
